title: Maximum Value of an Ordered Triplet II
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` (0-indexed). For three indices with `i < j < k`, define the triplet's value as `(nums[i] - nums[j]) * nums[k]`. Return the largest value any such triplet reaches, or `0` if every triplet's value is negative.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every triplet costs O(n³). Fix the middle index `j` instead: every value is positive, so the best `i` is the largest number to the left of `j`, and the best `k` is the largest number to the right of `j`. A prefix maximum and a suffix maximum give both in O(1), so each middle index is scored in constant time. When even the best difference is negative, the triplet is ignored because the answer never drops below `0`.

## Approach

1. Build `suffixMax` from the right: `suffixMax[k]` is the largest of `nums[k..n-1]`.
2. Start `prefixMax` at `nums[0]` and `best` at `0`.
3. For each middle index `j` from 1 to `n - 2`, compute `value = (prefixMax - nums[j]) * suffixMax[j + 1]` and keep the larger of it and `best`.
4. Only then fold `nums[j]` into `prefixMax`, so it serves later middles as a left end.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [12, 6, 1, 2, 7]` gives `suffixMax = [12, 7, 7, 7, 7]`. With `prefixMax = 12`:
- `j = 1`: `(12 - 6) * 7 = 42`, so `best = 42`.
- `j = 2`: `(12 - 1) * 7 = 77`, so `best = 77`.
- `j = 3`: `(12 - 2) * 7 = 70`, no change.

The answer is `77`, from indices (0, 2, 4).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to build `suffixMax` and one pass over the middles.
- Space: O(n) for `suffixMax`.

## Pitfalls

- Start `best` at `0`, not at the first triplet's value, so all-negative inputs return `0`.
- The right maximum must start at `j + 1`: on `[10, 9, 1]` using `nums[j]` itself as `k` would report `9` instead of `1`.
- Values reach about `10^12`, beyond 32-bit integers; Java and C need a 64-bit result.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `suffixMax` | `suffixMax[k]` is the largest value from index `k` to the end |
| `prefixMax` | largest value strictly before the current `j` |
| `j` | the middle index being scored |
| `value` | best triplet value with middle `j` |
| `best` | largest value found so far (at least `0`) |

narration.3: suffixMax[k] will hold the largest value from index k to the end.
narration.4: The last position's suffix maximum is just its own value.
narration.5: Fill the suffix maxima from right to left.
narration.6: Each entry is the larger of its own value and the maximum to its right.
narration.9: Before the first middle index, the largest left value is nums[0].
narration.10: Start at 0 because the answer is 0 when every triplet is negative.
narration.11: Try every possible middle index j; there must be room on both sides.
narration.12: Best left value minus the middle, times the best value to the right.
narration.13: Keep the larger of this middle's value and the best so far.
narration.14: Now nums[j] can serve as a left end for later middles.
narration.16: Return the best triplet value found.
